prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and the design of long-acting incretin-based therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: a single B014 prize to Drucker, Holst and Knudsen. After round 1 I rest the case on the chain of evidence, not on the six first-place opening ballots. Holst established GLP-1 secretion and action in humans, Drucker defined the proglucagon-derived peptide biology and its intestinotropic and metabolic actions, and Knudsen solved the pharmacokinetic problem of a peptide with a half-life of minutes through acylation and albumin binding, which produced liraglutide and semaglutide. The mechanism is stable and replicated, and large independent randomised trials show benefit in type 2 diabetes, obesity, and cardiovascular and renal disease. I read the round-1 exchange as showing that the real disagreement is about what the citation should name, since no one disputes the science. The citation therefore has to say plainly that it honours the physiology and its realisation as medicine, so that the committee records the reasoning and does not settle it by default.
statement.case_against: The weakest point is still the third name. Mojsov's identification and synthesis of the active truncated peptide is a credible claim, Habener's early proglucagon work sits outside the supplied credit list, and I cannot adjudicate the priority record from the materials I am allowed to read. My choice of Knudsen also means treating industrial drug design as part of a physiology-or-medicine discovery, which some colleagues, Wahren-Herlenius among them, reasonably reject as development. If the committee decides the prize should recognise discovery only, my trio is the wrong one and Drucker, Holst and Mojsov is the defensible alternative. A second reservation is that the long-term safety of the class is still being established, and I cannot check the latest outcome data from the supplied files.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius holds that Drucker, Holst and Mojsov is the cleaner discovery citation, that Knudsen's work is drug development on an established discovery, and that substituting him would make the prize a hybrid. She also says she would not block the Knudsen version.
responses.response: Her hybrid argument is the strongest objection to my configuration, and I have tested it. I do not think the hybrid is a defect, because the prize would then describe what happened: a hormone physiology that had been known for decades became a therapy only once the half-life problem was solved. Acylation to bind albumin was a conceptual step with a new therapeutic principle behind it, and it is the evidence base for every large outcome trial the case relies on. I also think the Mojsov claim, though real, is harder to separate from the physiology than the trio framing suggests, since the active forms were characterised in several laboratories at about the same time. I still hold that her configuration is defensible. My answer to the question of how to choose is that the citation should name both the physiology and the therapy, and the record should state that Mojsov and Habener were weighed and left out because of the three-person limit, not because the priority question was resolved against them.

responses.point: The chair moved from Drucker, Holst and Mojsov to Drucker, Holst and Knudsen, would accept Mojsov for Knudsen if the reasoning is stated, and argues that a contested edge is not a contested core because Holst and Drucker are secure under any reading.
responses.response: I agree with the contested-edge argument, and it is why I do not think the attribution problem should delay or weaken the choice of B014. Two of three places are secure on every reading in the six files, and only the third is open. I would add a condition: that argument does not make the third name unimportant, because it decides what kind of prize this is. I take your offer to accept either trio as a useful basis for the vote, and I will say the same of mine. One correction about the record. Your round-1 reply to me discusses a genetics-to-cure arc and B009, but my round-1 file argued no such candidate. B009 is not on the shortlist, so I am not proposing it and my position here concerns B014 alone.

responses.point: Perlmann prefers Knudsen, regards the Mojsov priority claim as less separable from the physiology, anchors the citation in physiology and therapeutic development, and says past Physiology or Medicine prizes have recognised translation that produced a new therapeutic principle.
responses.response: I agree on the substance and would stress one limit on the precedent argument. Prizes that recognised translation did so when the step created a new principle or modality, and I think long-acting acylated GLP-1 analogues meet that bar, since they changed what a peptide hormone can be as a drug. That is a narrower claim than saying drug development belongs in the prize in general, and I would want the citation to avoid language that suggests the latter. Where I am less sure than you is on separability. I cannot verify from the supplied materials that the active peptide was characterised independently of Mojsov's work, so I would not rest the case for Knudsen on that point. I rest it on the therapeutic principle and the evidence base.

responses.point: El-Manira, who also names Drucker, Holst and Knudsen, ranks B008 second with a trio of Deisseroth, Hegemann and Nagel, and treats it as a causal method of exceptional originality with emerging clinical use.
responses.response: I still regard optogenetics as one of the most consequential methods in experimental biology, and I keep it as an alternative. The chair asked whether a pairing with a second part is preferable. For B008 I have no allocation I can defend. Your trio leaves out Bamberg's early channelrhodopsin electrophysiology and, within the supplied six, Boyden and Miesenböck, and a split of six into three does not follow from the evidence. Pairing it with B014 would also use up the three-person cap on a part that is more contested than the part it was meant to supplement. That is the main reason I now prefer the single-part prize, not a conviction that two parts can never work.

responses.point: Linnarsson prefers Knudsen because Drucker and Holst already cover discovery and physiology, so replacing Knudsen would leave the translation unrecognised, and he calls the B016 SMN2 antisense credit the cleanest on the shortlist while noting narrower impact.
responses.response: I agree with the translation argument and with the point that each of the three names makes a distinct, non-overlapping contribution. I would not move B016 above B006, for the reason you give: the credit is clean but the impact rests on a single therapeutic story. The chair's question was whether a second part is preferable to a single prize. My answer from the six files is that no candidate offers a two-part pairing with a clean credit split. B006 is the closest, and Eshhar's absence from the credited names and the unclear boundary between Rosenberg's cell transfer and CAR design are not resolved. I therefore keep B006 as my first alternative and not as a second part.

uncertainties: Whether the committee records the third name as Knudsen (discovery and translation) or Mojsov (discovery only), and whether Habener's absence from the supplied credit list needs separate treatment.
Whether pharmaceutical design that created a new therapeutic principle counts as a discovery within a Physiology or Medicine citation; the committee should record its reasoning explicitly.
The latest long-term safety and outcome data for incretin therapies, which I cannot verify from the supplied materials.
Whether a two-part prize would be better than a single part; I could not find a second part with a defensible credit split among B006, B008, B016 and B031.
statement.conflict_note: No change from round 1. I have co-authored single-cell work with Sten Linnarsson and Jonas Frisén, and none of the shortlisted ballots concerns that work or those people. I identify no documented connection to any credited candidate on the shortlist, and shared Karolinska Institutet affiliation is not treated as one. I do not request recusal.
